1. Where/how does the platform SSH into or otherwise reach a game server VM to run commands (power on/off/restart, RCON commands, config writes)? Look at worker/index.ts, worker/game-control.ts, and anything under node-agent/ or lib/ related to gameservers, ssh, proxmox, or rcon. I need to know: does it SSH directly to the guest OS via its sshPort/ipAddress, or go through a node-agent HTTP API on the Proxmox host, or something else?

2. How is the actual Minecraft server process run inside the guest — systemd service, Docker container, docker-compose, a supervisor script? What's the service/container name convention (e.g. does it relate to hostname like "minecraft-qj4rxt")? Where do game server logs live inside the guest (log file path)?

3. How does `GAME_CONFIG` (family=minecraft variant=paper) get applied — i.e. when a customer switches the Minecraft "variant" from vanilla to paper (or similar), what does the code actually do? Does it download a new server jar (e.g. paper.jar) or swap a Docker image/env var? Is there any known way this could fail silently or need a restart to fully take effect? Look for the game-config application logic — search for "variant", "paper", "gameConfig", "_appliedVariant", "GAME_CONFIG" in worker/ and lib/.

4. How does `GAME_UPDATE` work (server.game_update action, worker's GAME_UPDATE job type)? What does it do to game files/jar, and could it leave the server in a stuck/broken state if the process was running during the update?

5. How is the public game port exposed — I found a PortForward DB row: publicPort 20052 -> guestPort 25565, protocol tcp, on node "node-4" whose public IP is 139.99.125.21. How does this port forward actually get realized on the host (iptables/nftables DNAT rule, referenced by `natChain` field on the Node model, e.g. "NXEON_FWD_N4")? Where's the code that programs this, and where would I check on the actual host to confirm the DNAT rule exists and is current for this specific server (public port 20052 -> guest 10.20.3.103:25565)?

6. Also check how the game subdomain (e.g. "wujiesmp.play.nxeon.cloud") resolves — lib/game-subdomain.ts — does it point at an SRV record targeting the node's public IP and the PortForward's publicPort? Confirm the expected connection flow: customer connects to wujiesmp.play.nxeon.cloud -> SRV lookup -> node public IP : port 20052 -> DNAT -> 10.20.3.103:25565 (guest Paper server).

Also tell me: what are the credentials/method to actually SSH to node-4 (139.99.125.21) as root or via the node-agent, and separately how to reach the guest VM 10.20.3.103 (SSH port 20023 per the DB Server row) — is there a known root password/key location, or does the platform tunnel through the Proxmox host? I need this to do a live, read-only investigation of the actual running state (docker ps / systemctl status / iptables rules / minecraft server logs) — I am NOT asking you to actually SSH anywhere, just to tell me the mechanism and where any credentials/keys are stored (env vars, DB fields, files) so I can do it myself afterward.

Report back concisely with file paths and relevant code excerpts (function names, line numbers) for each of the 6 points above, plus the SSH/credential mechanism info. Under 600 words plus short code excerpts.

452	 * bounded `find` over `roots`. Candidate paths are compile-time constants; the
453	 * returned hit is re-validated against the path allowlist before any caller uses

493	/** Parse a `key=value` / `key value` config into a lowercase-keyed map. */
494	function parseFlatConfig(text: string): Record<string, string> {
495	  const out: Record<string, string> = {};
496	  for (const line of text.split(/\r?\n/)) {
497	    const t = line.trim();
498	    if (!t || t.startsWith("#") || t.startsWith("//") || t.startsWith("!") || t.startsWith(";")) continue;
499	    let key: string;
500	    let val: string;
501	    const eq = t.indexOf("=");
502	    if (eq >= 0) {
503	      key = t.slice(0, eq).trim();
504	      val = t.slice(eq + 1).trim();
505	    } else {
506	      const sp = t.search(/\s/);
507	      if (sp < 0) continue;
508	      key = t.slice(0, sp).trim();
509	      val = t.slice(sp + 1).trim();
510	    }
511	    // Strip surrounding quotes.
512	    val = val.replace(/^"(.*)"$/, "$1").replace(/^'(.*)'$/, "$1");
513	    if (key) out[key.toLowerCase()] = val;
514	  }
515	  return out;
516	}

518	/** Pull `Key=Value` pairs out of Palworld's `OptionSettings=(...)` blob. */
519	function parsePalworldIni(text: string): Record<string, string> {
520	  const out: Record<string, string> = {};
521	  const idx = text.indexOf("OptionSettings=(");
522	  const open = idx >= 0 ? text.indexOf("(", idx) : -1;
523	  const close = open >= 0 ? text.indexOf(")", open) : -1;
524	  if (open < 0 || close < 0) return out;
525	  const inner = text.slice(open + 1, close);
526	  let cur = "";
527	  let inQuote = false;
528	  const pairs: string[] = [];
529	  for (const ch of inner) {
530	    if (ch === '"') inQuote = !inQuote;
531	    if (ch === "," && !inQuote) {
532	      pairs.push(cur);
533	      cur = "";
534	    } else cur += ch;
535	  }
536	  if (cur) pairs.push(cur);
537	  for (const p of pairs) {
538	    const eq = p.indexOf("=");
539	    if (eq < 0) continue;
540	    let v = p.slice(eq + 1).trim();
541	    v = v.replace(/^"(.*)"$/, "$1");
542	    out[p.slice(0, eq).trim().toLowerCase()] = v;
543	  }
544	  return out;

553	 * The password is used ONLY as a Source RCON packet body downstream — never a
554	 * shell argument — and the port is parsed to an integer (`parsePort`), so neither
555	 * value can inject anywhere.

557	export async function readRconCreds(conn: Client, spec: GameControlSpec): Promise<RconCreds> {
558	  const cfg = spec.rconConfig;
559	  if (spec.rcon !== "source" || !cfg) {
560	    return { ok: false, reason: `Remote console is not available for ${spec.label}.` };
561	  }
562	  const path = await remoteLocateFile(conn, cfg.candidates, cfg.findRoots, cfg.findName);

566	
567	  const map = cfg.kind === "palworld-ini" ? parsePalworldIni(text) : parseFlatConfig(text);

569	  if (cfg.enableKey) {
570	    const en = (map[cfg.enableKey.toLowerCase()] ?? "").toLowerCase();
571	    if (en !== "true" && en !== "1" && en !== "on") {
572	      return { ok: false, reason: `RCON is not enabled in ${spec.label}'s config — enable it and restart to use the console.` };
573	    }
574	  }
575	  const password = map[cfg.passwordKey.toLowerCase()] ?? "";
576	  if (!password) return { ok: false, reason: `No RCON password is set in ${spec.label}'s config.` };
577	  if (password.length > 256) return { ok: false, reason: "RCON password in the config looks malformed." };

586	
587	const RCON_TYPE_AUTH = 3;
588	const RCON_TYPE_EXEC = 2;
589	const RCON_TYPE_RESPONSE = 0;
590	const RCON_ID_AUTH = 0x1;
591	const RCON_ID_CMD = 0x2;
592	const RCON_ID_END = 0x2711; // sentinel id for the trailing empty packet
593	
594	function rconPacket(id: number, type: number, body: string): Buffer {
595	  const bodyBuf = Buffer.from(body, "ascii");
596	  const buf = Buffer.alloc(bodyBuf.length + 14);
597	  buf.writeInt32LE(bodyBuf.length + 10, 0); // size = id(4)+type(4)+body+2 nulls
598	  buf.writeInt32LE(id, 4);
599	  buf.writeInt32LE(type, 8);
600	  bodyBuf.copy(buf, 12);
601	  // two trailing NUL bytes already zero from Buffer.alloc
602	  return buf;
603	}

605	/**
606	 * Open a TCP channel to `host:port` on the game VM THROUGH the authenticated SSH
607	 * connection. The RCON port therefore never needs to be reachable off the box.
608	 */
609	export function forwardTcp(conn: Client, host: string, port: number, timeoutMs = 8000): Promise<Duplex> {
610	  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
611	    const timer = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error("Timed out opening RCON channel")), timeoutMs);
612	    conn.forwardOut("127.0.0.1", 0, host, port, (err, stream) => {
613	      clearTimeout(timer);
614	      if (err) return reject(err);
615	      resolve(stream as unknown as Duplex);
616	    });
617	  });
618	}

620	export type RconResult = { ok: true; response: string } | { ok: false; error: string };
621	
622	/**
623	 * Speak Source RCON over `stream`: authenticate, run `command`, and read the
624	 * (possibly multi-packet) response, using a trailing empty packet as the
625	 * end-of-response sentinel. Never throws — resolves an {ok,error} result. The
626	 * password is only ever a packet body; the command was validated by the caller.
627	 */
628	export function sourceRcon(stream: Duplex, password: string, command: string, timeoutMs = 8000): Promise<RconResult> {
629	  return new Promise((resolve) => {
630	    let acc = Buffer.alloc(0);
631	    let authed = false;
632	    let response = "";
633	    let done = false;
634	
635	    const finish = (r: RconResult) => {
636	      if (done) return;
637	      done = true;
638	      clearTimeout(timer);
639	      try {
640	        stream.end();
641	      } catch {
642	        /* best effort */
643	      }
644	      resolve(r);
645	    };
646	    const timer = setTimeout(
647	      () => finish(authed ? { ok: true, response } : { ok: false, error: "RCON timed out (no response)." }),
648	      timeoutMs
649	    );
650	
651	    stream.on("data", (chunk: Buffer) => {
652	      acc = Buffer.concat([acc, chunk]);
653	      while (acc.length >= 4) {
654	        const size = acc.readInt32LE(0);
655	        if (size < 10 || size > 4110) return finish({ ok: false, error: "Malformed RCON response." });
656	        if (acc.length < size + 4) break;
657	        const id = acc.readInt32LE(4);
658	        const type = acc.readInt32LE(8);
659	        const body = acc.slice(12, 4 + size - 2).toString("ascii");
660	        acc = acc.slice(4 + size);
661	
662	        if (!authed) {
663	          // The auth response is a type-2 (AUTH_RESPONSE) packet; id === -1 on failure.
664	          if (type === RCON_TYPE_EXEC) {
665	            if (id === -1) return finish({ ok: false, error: "RCON authentication failed (wrong password)." });
666	            authed = true;
667	            stream.write(rconPacket(RCON_ID_CMD, RCON_TYPE_EXEC, command));
668	            stream.write(rconPacket(RCON_ID_END, RCON_TYPE_EXEC, "")); // sentinel
669	          }
670	          // A leading empty RESPONSE_VALUE some servers send pre-auth is ignored.
671	        } else {
672	          if (id === RCON_ID_END) return finish({ ok: true, response });
673	          if (type === RCON_TYPE_RESPONSE) response += body;
674	        }
675	      }
676	    });
677	    stream.on("error", (e: Error) => finish({ ok: false, error: e?.message || "RCON connection error." }));
678	    stream.on("close", () => finish(authed ? { ok: true, response } : { ok: false, error: "RCON connection closed." }));
679	
680	    stream.write(rconPacket(RCON_ID_AUTH, RCON_TYPE_AUTH, password));
681	  });
682	}

684	/**
685	 * Full inline RCON round-trip on an already-open SSH connection: read creds from
686	 * the server's config, tunnel to 127.0.0.1:<port>, run one command. Callers guard
687	 * SANDBOX and ownership before reaching here.
688	 */
689	export async function runRcon(conn: Client, spec: GameControlSpec, command: string): Promise<RconResult> {
690	  const creds = await readRconCreds(conn, spec);
691	  if (!creds.ok) return { ok: false, error: creds.reason };
692	  let stream: Duplex;
693	  try {
694	    stream = await forwardTcp(conn, "127.0.0.1", creds.port);
695	  } catch (e) {
696	    return { ok: false, error: e instanceof Error ? e.message : "Could not open RCON channel." };
697	  }
698	  return sourceRcon(stream, creds.password, command);
699	}

710	/**
711	 * Tail the game service's recent logs. Resolves the unit from the family hints
712	 * (compile-time constants), then reads the last `n` journal lines; if journald has
713	 * nothing, falls back to a `.log` file under the data roots. Read-only.
714	 */
715	export async function readGameLogs(conn: Client, spec: GameControlSpec, n = 200): Promise<LogResult> {
716	  const lines = Math.min(Math.max(Math.trunc(n) || 200, 20), 500);
717	  const hints = spec.serviceHints.map(shq).join(" ");
718	  const roots = spec.dataRoots.map(shq).join(" ");
719	  const script = [
720	    `unit=""`,
721	    `for c in ${hints}; do systemctl cat "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 && { unit="$c"; break; }; done`,
722	    `if [ -z "$unit" ]; then unit=$(systemctl list-units --type=service --plain --no-legend 2>/dev/null | grep -i ${shq(spec.family)} | head -1 | awk '{print $1}'); fi`,
723	    `echo "NXLOG:UNIT:${"$"}{unit:-none}"`,
724	    `if [ -n "$unit" ]; then journalctl -u "$unit" -n ${lines} --no-pager 2>/dev/null; fi`,
725	    // Fallback: newest *.log under the data roots (bounded).
726	    `f=""; for r in ${roots}; do [ -d "$r" ] && f=$(find "$r" -maxdepth 4 -type f -name '*.log' 2>/dev/null | head -1) && [ -n "$f" ] && break; done`,
727	    `if [ -n "$f" ]; then echo "NXLOG:FILE:$f"; tail -n ${lines} "$f" 2>/dev/null; fi`,
728	  ].join("\n");
729	  const { stdout } = await exec(conn, script, QUICK_TIMEOUT_MS);
730	  const all = stdout.split(/\r?\n/);
731	  let unit: string | null = null;
732	  const out: string[] = [];
733	  for (const l of all) {
734	    const m = /^NXLOG:UNIT:(.*)$/.exec(l);
735	    if (m) {
736	      unit = m[1] === "none" ? null : m[1];
737	      continue;
738	    }
739	    if (/^NXLOG:FILE:/.test(l)) continue;
740	    out.push(l);
741	  }
742	  while (out.length && out[out.length - 1].trim() === "") out.pop();
743	  return { ok: true, lines: out.slice(-lines), unit };
744	}

## Multi-node synergy — how it works, and how to add node N

This is the standing reference for the architecture described above; update it as further phases of the
2026-09-05 rollout land; each phase should update this section in the same commit as its code, not after.

### The `Node` model, at a glance

One row per physical Proxmox host: `apiUrl`/`tokenId`/`tokenSecret` (a scoped Proxmox API token — every
VM-level operation goes through this, via `pveFor(conn)`/`pveForNode(node)` in `lib/proxmox.ts`, never
raw SSH), `publicIp`, `natChain`/`bridge`/`subnetPrefix` (this node's own NAT island — see below),
`provider`/`region`/`providerServerId`, `isPrimary`/`enabled`/`status`. Contrast with `HostingNode` (the
separate shared-hosting product), which has real SSH fields (`sshHost`/`sshPort`/`rootPasswordEnc`) —
a deliberate difference in trust model between the two products, not an inconsistency to "fix" by
converging them.

### The NAT-island principle

Each node NATs its **own** private `/24` (`10.20.N.0/24`) behind its **own** public IP. This makes each
node fully self-sufficient for provisioning, IP allocation, and SSH DNAT — but it does **not** give VMs
on different physical hosts a shared LAN. A VM on node-1 cannot reach a VM on node-2 over the private
network; they are separate NAT islands unless a future WireGuard/VXLAN overlay is built (not needed for
independent single-node-per-customer VPS/game hosting, which is the common case today).

### Standing rules for any new per-server code

1. **Any new Proxmox API call for a specific server must go through `pveFor`/`pveForNode`**, never the
   bare singleton functions in `lib/proxmox.ts` — those exist only as a same-behavior fallback for the
   (rare, and shrinking) case where a `Server` row genuinely has no `node` relation.
2. **Any new SSH/SFTP/RCON call site must select both `dedicatedIp` and `node`** on its `Server` query

   made three separate times, that all had to be found and unwound in the 2026-09-05 audit) — always go
   through `withServerSsh`/`exec` (`lib/ssh-exec.ts`).

## Nxeon game-server architecture — findings

**1. Transport: direct SSH to the guest, never node-agent.** All game-server control (power, RCON, config edits) goes over a direct SSH2 connection straight to the guest OS as `root`, using its stored root password. `lib/sftp.ts:connectionTarget()` (used everywhere via `lib/ssh-exec.ts:withServerSsh`) resolves host/port:
```ts
// lib/sftp.ts:148
const dedicated = !!server.dedicatedIp;
const host = dedicated ? server.dedicatedIp!.address : (server.node?.publicIp ?? process.env.PUBLIC_IP ?? "");
const port = dedicated ? 22 : server.sshPort;
```
Password: `serverRootPassword()` decrypts `Server.rootPasswordEnc` (AES via `lib/crypto-box.ts`, key = `AUTH_SECRET` env) falling back to legacy plaintext `rootPassword`. `node-agent/index.js` (HTTPS, bearer-token `NXEON_AGENT_TOKEN`) is a *separate* mechanism used only for **host-level** ops on non-primary Proxmox nodes (iptables NAT rules, cloud-init snippet writes) — never touches the guest OS and has no shell access (`worker/network.ts:agentNatHost`, docs §"Multi-node synergy" rule 3).

**2. Guest process model.** Minecraft/CS2/Palworld run as a systemd unit wrapping a `docker create` container (`worker/index.ts`'s `wrapDockerGameService()`), so systemd — not `docker --restart` — owns the lifecycle. Unit name resolved by hint from `lib/game-control.ts` `GAME_CONTROL.minecraft.serviceHints = ["minecraft","minecraft-server"]` (not hostname-derived — `minecraft-qj4rxt` naming isn't used; container name for Minecraft is fixed `mc`, `worker/game-config.ts:660`). Logs: `journalctl -u <unit> -n <N>`, fallback to newest `*.log` under `dataRoots` (`/opt/mc`, etc.) — `lib/game-control.ts:readGameLogs`.

**3. GAME_CONFIG / variant apply** (`worker/game-config.ts:gameConfigApply`): gated by `ENABLE_REAL_GAMECFG` or per-family `REAL_APPLY_FAMILIES` allowlist — production servers not in that allowlist get a **simulated** apply (DB marker only, no SSH) unless the flag is on, and the code explicitly used to lie about this being applied. For Minecraft, `variant` (paper/vanilla/etc.) is injected **only at provision time** as `-e TYPE=PAPER` (`worker/game-variant.ts:applyGameVariant`) into the `itzg/minecraft-server` image's setup script — it does not manually download a jar; the image itself fetches Paper on boot. Switching variant post-provision on a running server does **not** apply live at all — `gameConfigApply`/`applyRealConfig` has no variant-switch path for Minecraft (only VERSION triggers a container recreate). Most Minecraft settings write to `server.properties` then best-effort RCON-push (`tryMinecraftRcon`); RCON is admittedly missing (`mcrcon` not installed) on the current image, so **it silently falls back to "restart required"** — a known, called-out gap.

**4. GAME_UPDATE** (`worker/game-update.ts` + `lib/game-update-verify.ts:updateCommand`): SSHes in, runs `steamcmd +app_update <appId> validate`, then **always** `systemctl restart <unit>` if a fresh build was fetched (skips restart if already current — the code was previously buggy and restarted+disconnected players even when nothing changed). Verified via `NXGU:*` markers, not exit code. If the process was mid-write when steamcmd validates, this is an unattended live restart — brief downtime is the intended/accepted risk, not a stuck state (there's no run-time check that the world is safely saved first, beyond the restart itself).

**5. Port forwarding**: `lib/nat-rules.ts` computes intended DNAT rules from `PortForward` rows; `worker/network.ts:syncPortForwards()` reconciles per-node (`iptablesHost()` locally on primary, `agentNatHost()` via node-agent HTTPS on others) against `Node.natChain` (default `NXEON_FWD`, per-node e.g. `NXEON_FWD_N4`). To verify on node-4 host: `iptables -t nat -S NXEON_FWD_N4` (should show `-A NXEON_FWD_N4 -p tcp --dport 20052 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.20.3.103:25565`).

**6. Subdomain**: `lib/game-subdomain.ts` only handles subdomain *uniqueness* (DB checks), not DNS/SRV resolution — the SRV wiring lives elsewhere (`worker/game-subdomain-sync.ts`, not fully read but matches your described flow: subdomain → SRV → node public IP:publicPort → DNAT → guest:25565).

**SSH/credentials mechanism**: Guest VM (10.20.3.103, sshPort 20023) → `ssh -p 20023 root@139.99.125.21`, password = `Server.rootPasswordEnc` decrypted (needs `AUTH_SECRET`) or query via psql (documented runbook, docs/DOCUMENTATION.md ~line 3639). **The Proxmox host (node-4) itself has no SSH credential stored anywhere in this codebase** — VM lifecycle goes through the Proxmox API token (`Node.apiUrl/tokenId/tokenSecret` in DB, `lib/proxmox.ts`), and host-level shell ops go through `node-agent` (token in `/etc/nxeon/node-agent.env`, no shell exposed, only iptables/pvesm/snippet endpoints). Root access to the physical Proxmox box was set up manually by whoever ran `scripts/onboard-node.sh` on it — that credential is outside the app (provider console / operator's own key), not in the DB.
